_meta.purpose: Operational energy and carbon factors (LCA module B6), plus grid decarbonisation over the study period.
_meta.provenance_policy: All values PLACEHOLDER. Replace energy use intensities with measured or simulated figures for the actual building, and grid factors with Energimyndigheten / Naturvårdsverket published trajectories.
_meta.critical_note: The grid trajectory below is the reason operational and embodied carbon cannot be compared as a single number without stating a time horizon. Swedish electricity is already low-carbon and district heating is falling. Over a 50-year study period the embodied carbon of a transformation increasingly dominates the operational saving it delivers — so an energy retrofit that requires heavy new material can lose on carbon while winning on energy. The engine reports the two separately AND as a time-integrated total, and never lets one hide the other.

energy_use_intensity_kwh_m2_yr._note: Delivered energy after retrofit, by use. Care and event uses are higher than office per m² for different reasons: care runs 24/7, event runs at extreme peak density for few hours.

vacant._note: Vacancy is not free. A building kept warm and empty between uses still emits — which is an argument for short-horizon interim uses and belongs in every scenario timeline.

carbon_intensity_kgco2e_per_kwh._note: Year-indexed. Linear interpolation between anchor years; values held flat beyond the last anchor.

energy_price_sek_per_kwh._note: Used for operational cost. Real terms, excluding inflation, so it is comparable with undiscounted capital cost.

study_period.carbon_discounting_note: Carbon is deliberately NOT discounted while money is. Discounting future emissions embeds an ethical assumption that a tonne emitted in 2070 matters less than one emitted today — defensible for capital, not for atmospheric physics. State this choice in any publication; reviewers will ask, and it is a position rather than an oversight.
